question: What is the difference between session-based authentication and stateless JWT authentication?
reference_answer: Session-based auth stores session data (user ID, permissions) on the server (in memory, database, or Redis) and sends an opaque session ID cookie to the client; it allows instantaneous server-side session revocation but requires centralized session lookups. question: What is the difference between RabbitMQ and Apache Kafka and when would you choose each?
reference_answer: RabbitMQ is an AMQP message broker focusing on flexible routing (direct, fanout, topic exchanges), fine-grained message acknowledgments, and transient queue consumption where messages are deleted upon consumption. Active transactions read snapshots containing only tuples committed before their snapshot timestamp, allowing readers to never block writers and writers to never block readers.
